problem: RL agents learn from scratch, and existing uses of (V)LMs for control either ask the VLM for plans/actions (poorly grounded, bad at low-level control) or use it only as an instruction encoder, which under-uses its world knowledge and reasoning.
motivation: Embodied RL needs contextual representations that can index into task-relevant world knowledge. Even when a VLM's decoded text is wrong or cannot yield actions, its internal embeddings still hold useful semantic information, so prompting it with task-relevant questions can produce task-specific features that RL can ground into actions.
key_idea: Prompt a frozen generative VLM with task-relevant questions (not instructions) about each observation, and train an RL/BC policy on the resulting token embeddings (image, prompt and decoded text) as promptable representations.
insight: Prompting reshapes representations in a useful way: the same visual features perform much better when passed through a prompted VLM than when used as a generic image encoder (e.g. Minecraft combat spider 97.6 vs 51.2). Ablations show that removing the prompt or the text generation hurts, and that an oracle entity detector does not match PR2L, so it is not just detecting the entity. Chain-of-thought prompting adds common-sense features and lifts Habitat ObjectNav success from 27.8% to 41.9%. PCA shows PR2L embeddings are bimodal and cluster by room type, aligning with rewarding actions and value functions.
method: Promptable representations: for each observation, query a VLM with a task-relevant prompt, greedily decode or sample with a fixed seed, discard the text, and keep the last 2 layers' token embeddings for the image, prompt and decoded tokens.

Policy architecture: a learned encoder-decoder Transformer layer with a CLS token condenses the variable-length VLM token embeddings into one vector, which goes to an MLP (or LSTM in Habitat) along with pose and previous action. The VLM is frozen.

Task-relevant prompts: Minecraft uses 'Is there a [entity] in this image?', optionally with auxiliary text such as 'Spiders in Minecraft are black.'. Habitat uses 'Would a [target] be found here? Why or why not?' to elicit chain-of-thought.

Prompt evaluation proxy: candidate prompts are scored on a small labeled set by yes/no detection rate of the decoded answer and by linear probing of the embeddings, instead of running RL for each prompt.

Training: PPO online in Minecraft (InstructBLIP Vicuna-7B); behavior cloning on Habitat-Web human demos for ObjectNav (Prismatic Llama2-7B, Dino+SigLIP), with PCA to 1024 dims and pooled visual tokens; offline CQL/QR-DQN in a simplified Habitat setting.

setting.backbone: Frozen InstructBLIP Vicuna-7B (Minecraft) and Prismatic Llama2-7B Dino+SigLIP (Habitat) as feature extractors, plus a small policy (1-layer Transformer + MLP/LSTM) trained from scratch
setting.training_data: Minecraft: online PPO on 100k-150k env steps per task; Habitat: about 1.1M steps / 7,550 trajectories (~1/10 of Habitat-Web's 77k human demos) for BC; simplified Habitat: 2,364 trajectories of offline data
setting.observation: Egocentric RGB only (no depth), plus pose, previous action, and target object class (Habitat)
setting.action_space: Discrete: Minecraft turn/move/attack/use (53 or 89 actions); Habitat turn left/right 30°, move forward, stop

numbers.backbone: Prismatic Llama2-7B (frozen) + policy trained by BC
numbers.extra: Trained on ~1/10 of Habitat-Web demos; RGB only, no depth; 2000 val episodes; 40 epochs
numbers.evidence: Table Habitat ObjectNav results: Average (2000) With CoT 41.9%

numbers.backbone: Prismatic Llama2-7B (frozen) + policy trained by BC

numbers_note: Minecraft results are IQM success counts, not standard navigation metrics, so they are not listed. Habitat ObjectNav reports only success rate, with SPL not given. The simplified Habitat offline RL result (60.4% vs 35.2%) is on a custom setup.
results: PR2L beats all non-oracle baselines on all 6 Minecraft tasks (e.g. combat spider 97.6 vs 72.9 for the best of R3M/VC-1/RT-2-style, and milk cow 223.4 vs 128.6) and matches or exceeds Minecraft-specific oracles in half of the comparisons. On Habitat ObjectNav val-unseen, PR2L with CoT reaches 41.9% SR against 27.8% without CoT, 11.6% for the VLM image encoder, and at most 15.8% for VC-1. It does not reach VC-1's published 60.3%, which used over 10x more data.
limitations: Prompts are hand-crafted, and the quality of the representations depends heavily on the VLM (InstructBLIP could not reason about Habitat scenes).
VLM size and speed limit the approach (3-5 Hz inference), which slows online learning, and PR2L does not help exploration.
The Habitat evaluation uses only ~1/10 of the data and RGB-only inputs, and does not match published SOTA.
